description: A distinct, never-before-advanced timestamp that lands in the rule's currently open bucket is a genuine out-of-order write, not a duplicate-policy fold, even though the bucket has not closed yet: `TS.MADD fz:k0 1999 1` opens the [1500,2000) bucket (AGGREGATION last 500), then a separate `TS.MADD fz:k0 1500 0` back-fills the same still-open bucket with an earlier timestamp, then `TS.MADD fz:k0 2000 0` closes it. Streaming the 1500 write straight into the open `last` aggregator (call order) overwrites its value with 0; recalculating the bucket from source (timestamp order) correctly keeps last=1 from ts=1999, which is what RTS reports.
